extracted.intended_audience: prospective novel-writing certificate students / continuing-studies creative writers
extracted.subtask_description: Curriculum and program requirements for a two-year Novel Writing Certificate: course sequence (The Writing Life + Novel I–IV), one elective, and an optional one-on-one tutorial, with expectations for workshop submissions, manuscript progress, and program supports. Specifies timing, submission volumes, and administrative constraints for completing the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required course sequence for certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Year 1: Fall: The Writing Life (OWC 101); Winter: Novel I: The Powerful Beginning (OWC 303); Spring: Novel II: Plot and Structure (OWC 304); Year 2: Fall: Novel III: Subtext, Theme, and Language (OWC 305); Winter: Novel IV: Manuscript Completion and Revision (OWC 306).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sequence begins with The Writing Life followed by four Novel workshops that support drafting and revising manuscripts. The One-on-One Tutorial (OWC 310) is optional and not required to receive the certificate; it is available for one calendar year after completing Novel IV. Students should follow the prescribed order to prepare for workshop-centered Novel courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elective requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must complete one elective drawn from the open-enrollment Continuing Studies creative writing courses. The elective should focus on a particular genre or craft element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electives may be taken during the Summer break, concurrent with any Novel Writing Certificate courses, or up to a year after Novel IV. Examples include Poetry, Memoir, and courses focused on specific genres or craft elements. Electives must be taken for a letter grade. Courses taken through Stanford Continuing Studies within the past five years may be applied toward this requirement subject to the program director’s approval. Continuing Studies does not accept transfer credits; courses taken outside of this program (including at Stanford) will not meet the elective requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly submission volume expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first four courses, students can expect to submit a total of 6,000 to 7,500 words per quarter for feedback from both the instructor and their peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Novel 4, students workshop 10,000 to 12,000 words, allowing for sustained engagement with a longer section of the manuscript. Submission volumes are the basis for workshop feedback and are designed to balance regular progress with in-depth critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript length and completion expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Most published novels are between 70,000 and 85,000 words; students aiming to complete a full novel during the two-year sequence should continue drafting new chapters between workshop submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reaching novel length will require sustained drafting beyond what is submitted for workshop. Use deadlines as milestones while steadily building the manuscript toward completion; workshop submissions alone are unlikely to reach full-novel length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop feedback model
rubrics_metrics.description: Novel 1–4 focus on sustained progress on a full-length manuscript: students generate new pages, share them in workshops, and receive detailed feedback from both the instructor and their peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each course highlights craft questions that arise at different stages of a novel. Discussion of published novels and respected craft texts help illuminate how experienced authors handle challenges of structure, character, pacing, and thematic development.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Writing Life course focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The Writing Life (OWC 101) explores the fundamentals of novel design by reading published novels alongside selected craft texts while responding to generative prompts and sharing excerpts from works in progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course helps writers clarify the project they want to pursue and prepares them for the workshop-centered Novel sequence through reading, prompts, and early excerpt-sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft emphases by later courses (Novel III & IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novel III emphasizes subtext, theme, and language; Novel IV emphasizes manuscript completion and revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Later courses target craft questions appropriate to advanced stages of a manuscript (e.g., subtext, thematic cohesion, language choices, and sustained revision practices). Novel IV’s larger workshop submission enables sustained engagement with longer manuscript sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-on-One Tutorial procedure and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The One-on-One Tutorial (OWC 310) is an optional ten-week intensive revision tutorial: before the quarter begins the instructor will read the student’s entire novel draft and provide a developmental edit letter; during the term the student may revise up to 100 pages for feedback accompanied by scheduled meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each instructor-student pair will establish goals and a schedule of revision deadlines. Students may indicate instructor preferences and pairings are only finalized with the student’s approval. The tutorial is available only to Certificate students. Tuition covers manuscripts up to 85,000 words; a surcharge applies for manuscripts that exceed this length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tutorial availability timing
rubrics_metrics.description: OWC 310 is available for one calendar year after completing Novel IV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students must enroll in the One-on-One Tutorial within that one-year window after completing Novel IV if they wish to access the option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program supports for sustained writing practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructors may incorporate writing sprints, optional residencies, or other forms of structured writing time to help students maintain momentum and sustain a regular writing practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These practices are intended to help students move consistently toward their goals by providing structured time, accountability, and opportunities for intensive drafting amid the workshop schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community and post-program continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: The program seeks to foster a community of writers who will support one another after the program ends; instructors may help organize writing groups that continue meeting and exchanging work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many graduates report continuing to meet with peers from their cohort as beta readers and to celebrate publications and other successes; instructors may offer suggestions for how students can stay connected during breaks and beyond.
